Alpacas help families on the grassland.

Alpacas are helping families who raise animals on grassland in Inner Mongolia. A large breeding center there started in twenty thirteen with seventy-eight alpacas. Today, it keeps more than fifteen hundred female alpacas for breeding. The animals have become an important part of the business.

The center's manager says alpacas eat about half as much as sheep. This means that raising them can put less pressure on the grassland. Families can earn money from these animals while helping to protect the land they use.

Their thick hair, called fleece, is also useful. The manager says it is much warmer than ordinary wool. The company plans to grow slowly and invite local families to raise alpacas together. It hopes more people will share in this work as the breeding center develops.
